description: Barium is a chemical element with symbol Ba and atomic number 56, belonging to group 2 as the fifth element. It is a soft, silvery alkaline earth metal that is highly chemically reactive and never found in nature as a free element.
uses: Barium has been used as a getter in vacuum tubes, as an emissive coating on cathodes, and is a component of high-temperature superconductors and electroceramics. Barium compounds are added to fireworks for green color, barium sulfate is used in oil well drilling fluids and as an X-ray radiocontrast agent for imaging the gastrointestinal tract, and water-soluble barium compounds have been used as rodenticides.
characteristics: Barium is a soft, silvery-white metal with high electrical conductivity that rapidly oxidizes in air to form a dark gray layer. It has a Mohs hardness of 1.25, a melting point of 1,000 K, and a density of 3.62 g/cm³, adopting a body-centered cubic structure at room temperature.
